entity: Aeneas (predictingthepast.com), Google DeepMind's multimodal generative neural network for contextualizing Latin inscriptions, introduced in Nature on 23 July 2025 (Assael, Sommerschield et al.), co-developed with the University of Nottingham and with researchers at Warwick, Oxford and the Athens University of Economics and Business: it retrieves textual and contextual parallels from the Latin Epigraphic Dataset and restores, dates and places inscriptions; formalized in the Revelation First meta-aggregator record of 2026-10-30 (https://www.revelationfirst.com/aggregators/aeneas/). Distinct from Aeneas the Trojan hero, after whom it is named, and from Aeneas of Acts 9, homonyms of the bare name
row_type: C (a public entity on which the archive bears: an AI model for ancient inscriptions; an entity of the Revelation First meta-aggregator)

classes_note: Three classes, each the census's own intersection, kind, unit, text object or evidence kind for the entity, stated by field sources at the loci given: (1) AI models for ancient texts (census intersection 'ai-ancient-texts', evidence_kind 'machine reading, restoration or dating', worked question 'machine-dating'; B1, B5, B7); (2) parallels as evidence (census kind, unit, answers, does_not_answer; B1, B2, B3, B5); (3) Latin inscriptions (census text_object; B1, B3, B5). The archive bears on these classes through the Revelation First thesis (#202 and the deposits revelationfirst.com cites: parallels between Revelation and the other New Testament writings and the direction of their dependence), its Sappho and papyrological work, and its machine-reading work; a deposit enters only where its sentence says something of the entity or applies its category to one of these classes. The census's rf_intersection ('Parallels as evidence: the model retrieves the kind of evidence the midrashim transform argues from ...') is the archive's reading, ledgered as RF-; it does not by itself admit a deposit. Aliases: the name (case-sensitive; every hit is read, and uses of the hero, Virgil's Aeneas, or Aeneas of Acts 9 are the homonyms' and rejected), the interface's name and host (Predicting the Past, predictingthepast.com, a census aka) and the model's dataset (Latin Epigraphic Dataset). Ithaca, DeepMind's earlier Greek model, is a neighbour entity (census relation), not an alias; its string enters only class (1). Admission by reading (§3.4): a bare mention, a reference-list entry or a keyword is not a claim.
